__broaden__.ἐίσας: ἐΐσος — well-balanced, even (sense disputed, perhaps ’equal on both sides’); fem. acc. pl. ἐίσας, agreeing with νῆας · also fem. acc. pl. agreeing with δαῖτας: ’equal, fair (feasts)’ · also fem. acc. pl. agreeing with φρένας: ’well-balanced, sound (wits)’
__broaden__.περίφρων: περίφρων — circumspect, of sound understanding; fem. nom. sg., stock epithet of Penelope · also epithet of Arete: fem. nom. sg., ’the circumspect queen’
__broaden__.νόστοιο: νόστος — return home; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου), + gen. with τυγχάνω · also gen. governed by λανθάνω ’forget’ (νόστοιο λάθηται ’should forget his return’) · also gen. governed by χατίζων ’needing, longing for’ (νόστοιο χατίζων ’longing for his return’)
__broaden__.ὅτ: ὅτε (elided ὅτ’) — when; temporal conj., here + ἄν and subj. in a general/future clause · also + indic., of a single definite past event: ’when’ (ὅτ’ ἐν Ἄργεϊ ... ἵστασαν ’when they were mooring in Argos’) · also + opt., in a repeated past clause: ’whenever’ (ὅτ’ ἂψ ἄρχοιτο ’whenever he began again’) · also + subj. without ἄν, in a general clause: ὅτ’ … ἔχῃ ’whenever … holds’ · also in ὡς ὅτ’, ’as when (a minstrel does)’, the verb left unexpressed
__broaden__.σέο: σύ — you (sg.); gen. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic σοῦ), gen. of comparison · also possessive gen., ’your (own)’ (σέο τ’ αὐτοῦ κήδεα ’your own woes’)
__broaden__.αὐτοῦ: αὐτός — self; masc. gen. sg., intensive with a possessive (ἑὸν αὐτοῦ ’his own very own’): ’of himself’ · also the fixed adv. αὐτοῦ, ’there, on the spot, right here’ · also plain gen. sg. pronoun, unemphatic ’him’, governed by a preposition: ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ’from him’ · also intensive with a noun, masc. gen. sg.: ’Alcinous himself’ (αὐτοῦ Ἀλκινόοιο) · also reflexive intensive gen. sg. after a personal pronoun: σέο τ’ αὐτοῦ ’and of yourself’
__broaden__.λέγε: λέγω — gather, count, pick out (the Homeric sense, source of the later dominant sense ’say, tell’); impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔλεγε): ’was counting’ · also λέγω — say, tell; pres. imper. 2 sg.: ’tell’ (λέγε θέσκελα ἔργα ’tell the marvellous deeds’)
